forecast.revenue_drivers: FY2027E +88% to about $406bn: 1H FY2027 already delivered $177.8bn (+95.8% y/y) and Q2 data center revenue was $89bn (+117%), so the year is largely locked in (results, 2026-08-26); Q3 is guided to $108.0bn ±2%, about 12% q/q, explicitly with no China data center compute assumed (guidance, 2026-08-26). We assume Q4 grows roughly 11% q/q as Vera Rubin, now in full production, ramps alongside Blackwell Ultra, with hyperscale more than doubling y/y and ACIE up 138% y/y on AI natives, enterprises, sovereigns and AI clouds (2026-08-26). FY2028E +50%: first full year of Vera Rubin volume, networking attach (Q1 networking $14.8bn, +199% y/y; results, 2026-05-20), enterprise/sovereign AI clouds and over $500bn of third-party compute financing being mobilised (2026-08-26); the SB Energy/OpenAI 4.25GW PORTS-Pike campus (roughly $150-200bn of NVIDIA revenue per generation, first guarantee expected FY2029) contributes little before FY2029 (2026-08-26). FY2029E +30%: decelerating hyperscale capex growth and custom-ASIC competition (2026-11-08), with China data center compute still assumed at zero, partly offset by PORTS-Pike beginning to ship.
forecast.margin_drivers: FY2027E gross margin 74.5%: 1H ran 75.0% and Q3 is guided to 74.0% ±50bp (guidance, 2026-08-26); the prior-year $4.5bn H20 inventory charge does not repeat (results, 2026-05-20), but mix tilts to rack-scale systems and memory costs rise, with commitments up to $279bn from $119bn, primarily memory procurement (2026-08-26). Opex runs about 9% of revenue (Q3 GAAP opex ~$9.2bn, stepping up with the Vera Rubin launch, and SBC is now inside non-GAAP; 2026-05-20), giving a 65.5% operating margin. FY2028E 73.5% gross / 64.5% operating: HBM and packaging cost inflation plus systems mix, partly offset by scale and pricing; opex absorbs the Hugging Face deal ($11.9bn plus ~$1.0bn retention; 2026-09-03). FY2029E 72.5% gross / 63.0% operating: custom-ASIC competition and more normal pricing, plus depreciation on owned/guaranteed capacity, leave the opex ratio slightly higher.
forecast.vs_consensus: FY2027E revenue of about $406bn is 1.4% below consensus $411.7bn: consensus implies a Q4 near $126bn (+16.5% q/q) after the $108bn Q3 guide, whereas we hold Q4 to about +11% q/q because the guide excludes China data center compute and the Vera Rubin transition gates supply. FY2027E EPS of about $9.4 is modestly above consensus $9.31, on a 65.5% operating margin, a 16% tax rate and ~1.5% below-the-line income (normalised; FY2026's 5.1% included one-off gains). FY2028E is where we differ materially: about $609bn (+50%) versus consensus $692bn (+68.2%), and EPS ~$13.9 versus $15.91. Consensus extrapolates the +96% 1H FY2027 rate; we assume hyperscale capex growth decelerates through CY2027, China data center compute stays at zero, proprietary ASICs (Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta) take inference share (2026-11-08), and memory cost inflation trims gross margin to 73.5%. FY2029E +30% sits just below the DCF fade path of +35.3% on the same competition and digestion logic.
forecast.key_risk: The FY2028E growth rate is the assumption most likely to be wrong: we sit roughly 18pp below consensus while management describes demand as accelerating, with multiple frontier labs scaling in parallel (2026-08-26), so a fast Vera Rubin ramp plus conversion of the >$500bn financing platforms would push us toward consensus. Early tells are hyperscaler CY2027 capex guidance, Q4 FY2027 order/backlog commentary at the Q3 print, the $279bn of memory commitments and DSO, already 60 days versus 45 on extended terms with large investment-grade customers (2026-08-26). The second candidate is gross margin: if HBM pricing runs hotter than assumed, 73.5% in FY2028E is too high rather than too low.
forecast.remainder: The FY2027E revenue forecast implies revenue of 228,126mn for the second half (+82.3% year on year), against +95.8% reported so far this year. Consensus for those quarters (Q3 FY2027E + Q4 FY2027E) is 233,460mn, so our forecast is -2.3% versus the Street for the second half.

narrative.thesis: Does NVIDIA deliver consensus's FY2028 growth, or do custom ASICs, memory costs and the CEO probe cap it? Only partly: Hold. The price implies 40.4% revenue growth a year for five years; we model FY2028 revenue of 608,945mn against consensus 692,206mn, holding China data-center compute at zero and assuming proprietary ASICs take inference share. Beyond our years, the bull case needs the third-party compute-financing platforms to convert into Vera Rubin orders; the bear case is HBM inflation and a governance probe that delays customer decisions. Profit quality is worsening — cash conversion below profit, receivables outrunning sales, guarantees that shift customer credit onto NVIDIA. Our probability-weighted value of 175.13 is 6.2% below the price, so Hold; brokers underwrite the growth path we doubt.

narrative.company_overview:
NVIDIA designs accelerated-computing platforms — GPUs, networking and systems software — and sells them as data-center scale AI infrastructure. Two reported segments, Compute & Networking and Graphics, span data-center accelerators (Blackwell Ultra, with Vera Rubin now in full production), InfiniBand and Spectrum-X Ethernet networking, NVLink, RTX graphics, DRIVE Hyperion for autonomous vehicles and AI enterprise software.

Data Center was 89.7% of FY2026 revenue (193.7bn), Gaming 7.4%, Professional Visualization 1.5%, Automotive 1.1% and OEM & Other 0.3%; the United States was 69.3%, Taiwan 19.6% and Mainland China & Hong Kong 9.1%. Customers are hyperscalers, AI clouds, enterprises and sovereigns — a concentrated base whose capex plans lead NVIDIA's orders. Its edge is the CUDA software ecosystem plus a one-year product cadence; competition comes from AMD, Broadcom's custom accelerators and hyperscalers' own silicon.
narrative.financial_analysis:
1H FY2027 revenue was USD 177,837mn, up 95.8% year on year, gross margin 75.0% (1H FY2026: 66.6%) and net profit USD 118,010mn (+161.1%); the latest quarter alone grew 105.9% to USD 96,221mn. Free cash flow was USD 69,987mn and the balance sheet held net cash of USD 23,220mn at 26 Jul 2026.

Our forecast has FY2027E revenue of USD 405,963mn (+88.0%, 1.4% below consensus), FY2028E USD 608,945mn (+50.0% versus consensus USD 692,206mn) and FY2029E USD 791,629mn (+30.0%), with gross margin easing from 74.5% to 72.5% on memory costs and systems mix. The five-year record is margin-led — FY2026 net margin 55.6%, ROE 101.5% — but cash conversion has drifted to 0.86x and the accruals ratio to +10.9%.
narrative.valuation_overview: The rating rests on the probability-weighted scenario DCF — bear 107.56 (20%) on China scrutiny, the CEO probe and ASIC share, a 169.14 (50%) base and a 230.15 (30%) bull on the financing platforms converting — giving 175.13, 6.2% below the price; Buy needs 152.28. Cross-checks sit higher: the mechanical DCF 207.07 and peer-P/E 272.98, with peer-P/B excluded as an outlier. The reverse DCF shows the price already discounts 40.4% annual revenue growth for five years at a 39.0% FCF margin; the Monte Carlo median is 204.16, with 61% of draws above the price. The P/E on last fiscal-year EPS, 38.1x, is in the 6th percentile of its range.
narrative.competitive_analysis: NVIDIA compounds faster than any peer: TTM revenue growth of 105.9% against a 40.6% peer median, operating margin 66.2% versus 18.9%, and ROE 117.2% versus 30.4%. Gross margin was 74.7% on a TTM basis (75.0% in 1H FY2027), versus a 54.6% peer median. Growth and returns both come from the CUDA ecosystem, a one-year product cadence and networking attach; Broadcom is closest on margin, AMD on products. Valuation sits at a discount — 11.7x forward P/E versus a 17.2x peer median — after the multiple de-rated even as FY2028E consensus EPS rose 24.2% over 90 days.
narrative.news_summary: News splits between operating momentum and governance. Operationally, reports note revenue has nearly sextupled since Q3 2024, a record buyback, German startup investments, and caution that the largest customers want less reliance on NVIDIA; one report flags inventory turnover at a multi-year low of 3.35x. The dominant theme since the 6 November close is the board's investigation, with outside counsel, into whether CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation, following media reports of a relationship; the board said it has no reason to believe secrets were compromised. Shares fell pre-market on 9 November.
narrative.report_summary: Management guided Q3 FY2027 revenue to $108.0bn ±2%, about 12% higher sequentially, with GAAP gross margin of 74.0% ±50bp and opex near $9.2bn, explicitly assuming no China data-center compute (26 Aug 2026). CEO Jensen Huang said demand is accelerating across multiple frontier labs and that Vera Rubin is in full production. Events: the Hugging Face acquisition for roughly $11.9bn (2 Sep 2026), $105bn-capped guarantees on SB Energy's 4.25GW PORTS-Pike campus leased to OpenAI (17 Aug 2026), commitments of $279bn mostly for memory, and partnerships intended to mobilise over $500bn of third-party compute capital. Policy: US scrutiny of China distribution channels continues; the 10-Q warns controls on Chinese-origin models could materially affect the business. The 10-K flags supply, competition and customer-concentration risks.

narrative.rating_rationale: Fair value of 175.13 is 6.2% below the USD 186.64 price, so the rating is Hold. It comes from our probability-weighted scenarios — 20% bear at 107.56, 50% base at 169.14, 30% bull at 230.15 — with low confidence from a 24%-of-value spread and peer multiples 64% above our value. learner.big_picture: NVIDIA designs the chips that power artificial-intelligence data centres; Data Center is 89.7% of revenue. Sales rose 105.9% in the latest quarter versus a year earlier, and in FY2026 profit was 55.6% of sales. But the USD 186.64 price implies 40.4% growth a year for five years. We see FY2028 (the next fiscal year) growth halving: revenue of 608,945mn against analysts' consensus of 692,206mn. Cash is arriving slower than profit. Our blended value across scenarios is USD 175.13, 6.2% below the price, so the rating is Hold.

steps.business: Almost nine in every ten dollars of sales come from Data Center chips. 69.3% of revenue is booked in the United States. That is a concentrated business: gaming, automotive and other lines are small. The USD 4.51tn market value already assumes AI chip leadership continues. Next, check customer concentration in the annual report: a few large cloud buyers may dominate those sales.
steps.growth: Growth is still speeding up. The latest quarter rose 105.9% on a year earlier, faster than 95.8% for the half year. Peers grew 40.6% over the same twelve months. The fiscal-year rates tell older history, sliding from +125.9% to +65.5%, and the base is now far larger. Analysts expect +90.6% for this fiscal year. Check the third-quarter guide of USD 108.0 billion, which assumes no China data-center compute.
steps.profit: Margins are extraordinary. The FY2026 operating margin was 60.4%, roughly USD 60 per USD 100 of sales, against 37.3% in FY2022. But profit runs ahead of cash: cash conversion was 0.86x, meaning 86 cents arrived per dollar booked. Receivable days (how long customers take to pay) rose to 60 from 45 in the latest quarter. The company's adjusted profit now includes stock-based pay (shares given to staff). Check collections.
steps.safety: Net cash was USD 23,220mn at 26 July 2026, so cash beats debt. That is less than the USD 41,202mn at FY2026; total debt was USD 33,366mn then. Interest cover of 503.4x means operating profit dwarfs the interest bill. The warning sits off the balance sheet: guarantees capped at USD 105 billion for an OpenAI data-centre campus. If OpenAI cannot pay its leases, NVIDIA may have to.
steps.cheap: Trailing P/E (price divided by the past year's profit per share) is 23.6x, below the peer median of 42.0x. On next year's forecast it is 11.7x against 17.2x: two bases, reported versus expected profit. Price to book (price against net assets) is 19.7x, far above peers, so the discount is in earnings, not assets. A low multiple on record profit can warn that the market expects profit to fall.
steps.worth: Our scenarios, weighted by probability, give USD 175.13 a share. That is 6.2% below the USD 186.64 price, the value behind the Hold. Our base scenario is USD 169.14, our own forecast. The model's mechanical DCF (a formula-based check) of USD 207.07 is not our base case. The price implies growth of 40.4% a year for five years. Bear USD 107.56 to bull USD 230.15 shows the spread.
steps.others: All 30 brokers are positive; their median target is USD 322.50, 72.8% above the price. Eight targets are older than 90 days. Brokers rarely say sell, so treat targets as opinions. Our fair value of USD 175.13 is below even the lowest target, USD 275.00. A gap this size means we and the brokers assume different things. Ask which assumption differs.
steps.wrong: The stock fell 0.5% over a year while the S&P 500 rose 9.8%. Its largest fall from high to low was 24.1%. Volatility (how much the price swings) is 38.4%. Options priced a move of ±10.9% around the 17 November results. The data checks passed but flagged enterprise value, model versus brokers and AI commentary. Press reports of a CEO board review came after the price date.

discussion: The price implies 40.4% revenue growth a year for five years. What evidence would convince you that growth halves instead?
Cash conversion is 0.86x and receivable days rose to 60. Which would you check first, and why?
Brokers' median target is USD 322.50 and our fair value is USD 175.13. Which assumption would you test before trusting either?

company.description: NVIDIA Corporation operates as a data center scale AI infrastructure company in the United States, Taiwan, China, Hong Kong, Europe, and internationally. It operates through Compute & Networking, and Graphics segments. The Compute & Networking segment provides data center accelerated computing and networking platforms and artificial intelligence solutions and software, and automotive platforms and autonomous and electric vehicle solutions, including software. The Graphics segment offers GeForce GPUs for gaming and PCs; Quadro/NVIDIA RTX GPUs for enterprise workstation graphics. The company's products are used in gaming, professional visualization, data center, and automotive markets. It sells its products to original equipment manufacturers, original device manufacturers, system integrators and distributors, independent software vendors, cloud service providers, add-in board manufacturers, distributors, automotive manufacturers and tier-1 automotive suppliers, and other ecosystem participants. It has a collaboration with Cisco to develop Ultra-Dense Small Form Factor Pluggable (USFP), a high-density optical module pluggable transceiver. It has a collaboration with ChipAgents to develop Build-A-Chip-Bench, a benchmark for AI agents carrying chip design tasks and The Company has a strategic alliance with MediaTek to build the next generations of AI computing platforms. NVIDIA Corporation was incorporated in 1993 and is headquartered in Santa Clara, California.
